title: Wolves killed 1163 reindeer in Lapland this year
seoTitle: Wolves killed 1163 reindeer in Lapland in 2026
description: By 18 November 2026 Lapland's herding districts had recorded 1163 reindeer killed by wolves, and the wolf now does more damage up here than the wolverine.
dek: Wolves also took 53 dogs in Finland in the twelve months to 23 November, which is reason enough to keep a dog on the leash in reindeer country.
heroAlt: An open frost-covered mire under a deep blue sky, pale grass and low heath in the foreground, a line of frosted birches and pines on the horizon and a power line crossing the view, with a low sun burning at the right edge.
heroCaption: Frost on an open mire between Inari and Kaamanen in October 2026. The reindeer losses are recorded across the herding districts of Lapland, not at any single place.

body.text: The statistics of the Finnish Food Authority show 1163 reindeer killed by wolves in the herding districts of Lapland by 18 November 2026. According to Lapin Kansa the figure is a record, and more hunting dogs than before have been taken by wolves this year.

The wolf has also passed the wolverine as the large carnivore that does the most damage in the reindeer herding area. The game damage register at riistavahingot.fi, which covers the whole country, holds 1912 reindeer lost to wolves between 24 November 2025 and 23 November 2026, worth 3 273 398 euros. Wolverines account for 1617 reindeer in the same period, lynx for 1032 and bears for 912.

Most of what the wolves take is breeding stock. Of the reindeer killed by wolves, 1537 were breeding females and 177 were the calves of breeding stock, and 17 are listed under the register's own heading for tourism reindeer.
The wolves do not live up here, they pass through

In March 2026 there was most likely not a single wolf pack or pair holding a territory anywhere in the reindeer herding area, the Natural Resources Institute Finland estimates. In the autumn of 2025 there had been three such territories, two of them with a family pack. During the winter 34 wolves were removed from the herding area on damage-based permits, and most of them were shot outside the autumn territories. The whole country held an estimated 430 wolves in March.

A wolf kills reindeer all year round wherever it happens to be moving, says the Reindeer Herders' Association, and the heaviest damage falls on the eastern side of the herding area, where wolves make effective use of the border country and the Russian population behind it. Reindeer and wolves cannot share the same ground for long, the association says, because a reindeer is too easy a catch and the losses climb fast.
If you are out with a dog

A wolf treats a dog as an intruder on its territory, says Mikko Jokinen, large carnivore planner at the Finnish Wildlife Agency. The state compensates 35 to 55 dogs hurt or killed by wolves every year, and the register counted 53 dogs in the twelve months to 23 November. The dogs at the greatest risk are the ones working alone far from their owner, which in Lapland means a hunting dog rather than a dog on a hiking trail.

items: Keep your dog on the leash in the forest, or leash it the moment you see a large carnivore.
Make noise as you walk so the animal has time to move off. Rain, snowfall and strong wind cover the sound of a walker.
Do not leave a dog working loose once the light has gone.
Check what has been seen in the area from Luke's Luonnonvaratieto service, from local people and from the area's large carnivore contact person.
Call 112 if you meet a large carnivore that does not flee and the situation feels threatening.

body.text: If you do meet a wolf, let it know you are there by shouting or clapping your hands, then walk away calmly and do not run. If the wolf follows, keep going, shout or roar now and then and make yourself as big as you can by raising your arms. An attack is rare, and if one comes, the advice is to fight back as loudly and as hard as you can.

Sightings are worth passing on to the area's large carnivore contact person, and tracks are easiest to read in snow: photograph the print with a familiar object beside it for scale and measure the distance between strides as well. If a wolf does attack a dog, the owner has to tell the local rural livelihood authority and the game management association straight away, because compensation is paid only after officials have inspected the site.
A large carnivore avoids people by instinct, but it can be caught by surprise, and a sick or injured animal may behave in a threatening way.
Wolves, wolverines, lynx and bears all live in the same forests that visitors walk in, and knowing which of them you are likely to run into is worth more than any single number.
